# SK0209 — The expression parentheses are not arranged

<!-- Generated from Rules/Rikarin.Skala.Rules.Metadata/rules.json. Do not edit. -->

`skala arrange` would remove redundant parentheses.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | Formatting |
| Default severity | suggestion |
| Scope | Syntax |
| Needs a compilation | no |
| Fix | no |
| Language version floor | — |
| Since | 2.0 |

## Why

Parenthesis removal is the arranger's highest-risk syntactic cleanup, so each removal is proved rather than computed: the parentheses go only when the expression printed without them parses back to the same tree. Which redundant parentheses Skala is willing to lose is a separate, configured question — `skala_parentheses_redundancy_style` and the three `dotnet_style_parentheses_in_*_binary_operators` keys decide it. It runs by default; there is no opt-in flag.

## Example

Instead of:

```csharp
return (value);
```

Write:

```csharp
return value;
```

## When it does not fire

None relative to the effective configuration: a removal that would change the parse is refused by construction. Parentheses the configuration keeps for clarity remain — around the operands of shift and bitwise operators, and around a nested `&&`, `||` or `??` under `always_for_clarity` — and so do parentheses around an assignment, a conditional, a lambda, a query or a `switch` expression, inside an interpolation, or after a cast-shaped `(A)(b)`. Formatter-off regions are excluded. To keep every parenthesis, exclude the rule with `skala arrange --exclude SK0209`.

## Configuration

- `skala_parentheses_redundancy_style`
- `dotnet_style_parentheses_in_arithmetic_binary_operators`
- `dotnet_style_parentheses_in_relational_binary_operators`
- `dotnet_style_parentheses_in_other_binary_operators`
